# Measured on the real WDMCH, 2026-10-02, via SSH as dietpi@192.168.1.2.
# Read-only: blkid and lsblk only. Nothing was written to this machine.
#
# This file is the fixture the in-use-partition test runs against. It is
# recorded data, not a guess, and it is what makes the refusal test meaningful:
# the synthetic indexes prove the logic, these values prove the logic matches
# the machine the project is for.
#
# blkid -o export, one device per invocation.
#
#   sda19  LABEL="SWAP"    TYPE="swap"               PARTLABEL="SWAP"
#   sda20  LABEL="(none):1" TYPE="linux_raid_member"  PARTLABEL="SYSTEM"
#   sda21  LABEL="DATA"    TYPE="btrfs"              PARTLABEL="DATA"
#
# The one that matters:
#
#   sda20  UUID="dddddddd-1111-1111-1111-1111aaaaaaaa"
#          TYPE="linux_raid_member"  PARTLABEL="SYSTEM"
#          TYPE="swap"               PARTLABEL="SWAP"      <- sda19
#
# and /proc/mdstat:
#
#   md1 : active raid1 sda20[0]
#         20954112 blocks super 1.2 [2/1] [U_]
#
# /dev/md1 is the root filesystem:
#
#   findmnt: /dev/md1 on /     ext4  LABEL=SYSTEM
#   /          contains /nix /guix /etc/fido /var/spool/fido   5.9G used
#   3 running fido units: fidonet-bbs, fidonet-inotify, fidonet-telegram
#
# [2/1] means the array expects two devices and has one. p20 SYSTEM_B is the
# only member of the array backing the running root filesystem, so writing to
# p20 would take the system with it.

sda19  swap               SWAP     SWAP     [SWAP]
sda20  linux_raid_member  (none):1 SYSTEM
sda21  btrfs              DATA     DATA     /data
